title: Reading Drill — Recording historic street names — Reviewing the evidence
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Recording historic street names — Reviewing the evidence
passages.body:
**A** The town archivist in Brackenton received an old report about names disappearing from signs when roads are rebuilt. The report compared the number of names retained, but some entries had been collected under different conditions. To check the report, reviewers returned to the property registers rather than treating the published figures as a complete record.

**B** The review covered eight weeks. In the first part of that period, the original records did not consistently include mergers of adjacent streets. In the later part, the recording sheet included a separate field for it. The reviewers kept readings from both periods, but marked which items were missing rather than guessing what had happened.

**C** The conclusion listed a register of alternate names as a possible later response. It recommended collecting another set of readings before deciding whether to use it. The new data would be published with the method, so another group could work out whether its own measurements were comparable.
